parts.text:
Determine the simplest whole number ratio of the volumes of dilute hydrochloric acid R used
in Experiment 2 and Experiment 3.

parts.text:
Use your ratio in (b) to deduce the volume of dilute hydrochloric acid Q needed when
Experiment 1 is repeated using thymolphthalein indicator instead of methyl orange indicator.
volume of hydrochloric acid Q = ______

parts.text:
Compare the concentration of dilute hydrochloric acid Q used in Experiment 1 to the
concentration of dilute hydrochloric acid R used in Experiment 2.
Explain your answer.

State how the results change, if at all, if the aqueous sodium hydroxide is warmed before
adding the dilute hydrochloric acid. Give a reason for your answer.
effect on results ______
reason ______

parts.label: (i)
parts.text:
After the burette was filled with dilute hydrochloric acid at the start of Experiment 1, some of
the acid was run out of the burette.
One reason for running the acid out of the burette is to make sure the level of the hydrochloric acid
is on the scale.
Give one other reason why it is important to run some acid out of the burette after it has been
filled for the first time in an experiment.

text: You are going to investigate the reaction between aqueous sodium hydroxide and two different
solutions of dilute hydrochloric acid with different concentrations, labelled Q and R, using two
different indicators.
Read all of the instructions carefully before starting the experiments.
Instructions
You are going to do three experiments.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
State the colour change that occurred when distilled water was added to solid S to form
solution T.
from solid S ______ to solution T ______

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Test the pH of the first portion of solution T.
pH = ______

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
To the second portion of solution T, add the strip of magnesium ribbon.
Record your observations.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text:
To the third portion of solution T, add the aqueous potassium iodide.
Keep the product for use in (ii).
Record your observations.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text:
To the product from (i) add the aqueous sodium thiosulfate. Gently shake the test-tube.
Record your observations.

parts.label: (e)
parts.text:
To the fourth portion of solution T, add about 1cm depth of dilute nitric acid followed by a few
drops of aqueous barium nitrate.
Record your observations.

parts.label: (f)
parts.text:
To the fifth portion of solution T, add about 1cm depth of dilute nitric acid followed by a few
drops of aqueous silver nitrate.
Record your observations.

parts.label: (g)
parts.text:
To the sixth portion of solution T, add aqueous ammonia dropwise and then in excess.
Record your observations.

parts.label: (h)
parts.text: Identify solid S.

text: You are provided with solid S.
Do the following tests on solid S, recording all of your observations at each stage.
tests on solid S
To the boiling tube containing solid S add about 20cm of distilled water. Stopper the boiling tube and
shake the mixture to dissolve solid S and form solution T. Divide solution T into six approximately
equal portions in six test-tubes.
When solution A and solution B are mixed they react slowly to form iodine.
Starch solution is added to the mixture to act as an indicator.
When a certain amount of iodine is made there is a sudden colour change to blue-black.
Plan an investigation to find the effect of temperature on the rate of the reaction between solution A
and solution B.
You are provided with solution A, solution B, starch solution and common laboratory apparatus.
